A.subject: Physics
A.text: A ray of light entering from air into a denser medium of refractive index 4/3, as shown in figure. The light ray suffers total internal reflection at the adjacent surface as shown. The maximum value of angle θ should be equal to:
A.sol_text: By Snell's law at first surface: sin(θ)/sin(θ') = 4/3, so sin(θ') = 3sin(θ)/4. For total internal reflection at second surface: sin(θ'') > sin(θ_c), where θ'' = 90° - θ'. This gives sin(90° - θ') > sin(θ_c), so cos(θ') > 3/4. Using 1 - sin²(θ') > 9/16 with sin(θ') = 3sin(θ)/4, we get 1 - 9sin²(θ)/16 > 9/16. Simplifying: 7/16 > 9sin²(θ)/16, so sin²(θ) < 7/9, giving sin(θ) < sqrt(7)/3. Therefore sin(θ) = sqrt(7)/3.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: In the given potentiometer circuit arrangement, the balancing length AC is measured to be 250 cm. When the galvanometer connection is shifted from point (1) to point (2) in the given diagram, the balancing length becomes 400 cm. The ratio of the emf of two cells, e1/e2 is:
A.sol_text: e1 = 250 × Potential Gradient. e1 + e2 = 400 × Potential Gradient. Therefore, e1/(e1 + e2) = 250/400 = 5/8. By solving above, e1/e2 = 5/3

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A balloon was moving upwards with a uniform velocity of 10 m/s. An object of finite mass is dropped from the balloon when it was at a height of 75 m from the ground level. The height of the balloon from the ground when object strikes the ground was around: (takes the value of g as 10 m/s^2)
A.sol_text: Body is dropped from height 75m with initial velocity (upward) 10 m/s. Using s = ut + (1/2)at^2: -75 = 10t - (1/2)(10)t^2, which simplifies to 5t^2 - 10t - 75 = 0. Solving gives t = 5 sec. In 5 seconds, the balloon (moving upward at 10 m/s) covers: h = 10 × 5 = 50 m. Total height of balloon = 75 + 50 = 125 m

A.subject: Physics
A.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
A.text: An electron moving with speed v and a photon moving with speed c, have same de-Broglie wavelength. The ratio of kinetic energy of electron to that of photon is:
A.sol_text: For electron: de-Broglie wavelength λ_e = h/p = h/(mv), Kinetic energy KE_e = (1/2)mv^2 = pv/2. For photon: de-Broglie wavelength λ_p = h/p, Kinetic energy KE_p = pc. Given λ_e = λ_p, so h/(mv) = h/p_p, which gives p_p = mv. Since KE_p = pc = mvc, the ratio KE_e/KE_p = (pv/2)/(pc) = (mv*v/2)/(mvc) = v/(2c).

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Two vectors X and Y have equal magnitude. The magnitude of (X - Y) is n times the magnitude of (X + Y). The angle between X and Y is:
A.sol_text: Given: |X| = |Y| and |X - Y| = n|X + Y|. Squaring: |X - Y|^2 = n^2|X + Y|^2. Expanding: X^2 + Y^2 - 2X·Y = n^2(X^2 + Y^2 + 2X·Y). Since |X| = |Y|, let |X|^2 = |Y|^2 = a. Then: 2a - 2X·Y = n^2(2a + 2X·Y). Simplifying: (1 - n^2)(2a) = (1 + n^2)(2X·Y). Therefore: X·Y = ((1 - n^2)/(1 + n^2))a. Since X·Y = |X||Y|cos(theta) = a·cos(theta), we get: cos(theta) = (1 - n^2)/(1 + n^2) = -(n^2 - 1)/(n^2 + 1). Thus: theta = cos^(-1)((n^2 - 1)/(-n^2 - 1))

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Two ideal electric dipoles A and B, having their dipole moment p_a and p_b respectively are placed on a plane with their centres at O as shown in the figure. At point C on the axis of dipole A, the resultant electric field is making an angle of 37° with the axis. The ratio of the dipole moment of A and B, p_a/p_b is: (take sin 37° = 3/5)
A.sol_text: At point C on the axis of dipole A: E_1 = k(2p_a)/r^3 (axial direction). Dipole B is perpendicular to the axis, so at C: E_2 = k(p_b)/r^3 (equatorial direction). The resultant field makes 37° with the axis, so tan(37°) = E_2/E_1. Given tan(37°) = 3/4, we have: (p_b/r^3)/(2p_a/r^3) = 3/4, which gives p_b/(2p_a) = 3/4, therefore p_a/p_b = 2/3.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A 10 ohm resistance is connected across 220 V - 50 Hz AC supply. The time taken by the current to change from its maximum value to the rms value is:
A.sol_text: For AC current I = I_0 cos(ωt). The current changes from maximum value I_0 to rms value I_0/sqrt(2). Setting I_0/sqrt(2) = I_0 cos(ωt), we get cos(ωt) = 1/sqrt(2), which gives ωt = π/4. With ω = 2π × 50 Hz, solving for t: 2π × 50 × t = π/4, therefore t = 2.5 ms.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The relation between time t and distance x for a moving body is given as t = mx^2 + nx, where m and n are constants. The retardation of the motion is: (Where v stands for velocity)
A.sol_text: Given t = mx^2 + nx. Taking derivative: dt/dx = 2mx + n. Velocity v = dx/dt = 1/(2mx + n). Acceleration a = v(dv/dx) = v · (-2m)/(2mx + n)^2 = -2mv^3. Therefore retardation (magnitude) = 2mv^3

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A prism of refractive index μ and angle of prism A is placed in the position of minimum angle of deviation. If minimum angle of deviation is also A, then in terms of refractive index value of A is:
A.sol_text: At minimum angle of deviation, the ray passes symmetrically through the prism. Using the formula for refractive index: μ = sin((A + δm)/2) / sin(A/2). Given that δm = A, we substitute: μ = sin((A + A)/2) / sin(A/2) = sin(A) / sin(A/2) = 2sin(A/2)cos(A/2) / sin(A/2) = 2cos(A/2). Therefore, A = 2cos^(-1)(μ/2).

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Consider a planet in some solar system which has a mass double the mass of earth and density equal to the average density of earth. If the weight of an object on earth is W, the weight of the same object on the planet will be:
A.sol_text: Given: Mass of planet M_p = 2M_e, Density of planet ρ_p = ρ_e. Using g = (4/3)πRρG, we have g ∝ Rρ. Since ρ_p = ρ_e, we get g_p/g_e = R_p/R_e. From M = (4/3)πR^3ρ, we have 2M_e = (4/3)πR_p^3ρ_e and M_e = (4/3)πR_e^3ρ_e. Dividing: 2 = (R_p/R_e)^3, so R_p/R_e = 2^(1/3). Therefore g_p/g_e = 2^(1/3), and W' = 2^(1/3)W.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A force F = (40i + 10j) N acts on a body of mass 5 kg. If the body starts from rest, its position vector r at time t = 10s, will be:
A.sol_text: Step 1: Calculate acceleration a = F/m = (40i + 10j)/5 = 8i + 2j m/s^2. Step 2: Use kinematic equation r = u*t + (1/2)*a*t^2. Since body starts from rest, u = 0. Step 3: r = 0 + (1/2)*(8i + 2j)*10^2 = (1/2)*(8i + 2j)*100 = 400i + 100j m.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Two ions having same mass have charges in the ratio 1 : 2. They are projected normally in a uniform magnetic field with their speeds in the ratio 2 : 3. The ratio of the radii of their circular trajectories is
A.sol_text: Given: q1:q2 = 1:2, v1:v2 = 2:3, m1 = m2. Using radius formula r = mv/(qB), we have r1/r2 = (m1/m2) × (q2/q1) × (v1/v2) = 1 × (2/1) × (2/3) = 4/3. Therefore r1:r2 = 4:3

A.subject: Physics
A.text: If q_f is the free charge on the capacitor plates and q_b is the bound charge on the dielectric slab of dielectric constant k placed between the capacitor plates, then bound charge q_b can be expressed as:
A.sol_text: E_net = E_0/k, q_b = q_f(1 - 1/k). The bound charge on the dielectric slab is given by the relationship between free charge and the dielectric constant, where the bound charge reduces the net electric field by a factor of k.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Two spherical soap bubbles of radii r1 and r2 in vacuum combine under isothermal conditions. The resulting bubble has radius equal to:
A.sol_text: Given: Pressure outside is 0. Using P1*V1 + P2*V2 = P*V where P = 4T/r (pressure due to surface tension). For bubble 1: P1 = 4T/r1, V1 = (4/3)*pi*r1^3. For bubble 2: P2 = 4T/r2, V2 = (4/3)*pi*r2^3. For resulting bubble: P = 4T/r, V = (4/3)*pi*r^3. Substituting: (4T/r1)*(4/3)*pi*r1^3 + (4T/r2)*(4/3)*pi*r2^3 = (4T/r)*(4/3)*pi*r^3. Simplifying: (4T/3)*pi*(r1^2 + r2^2) = (4T/3)*pi*r^3/r. This gives: r1^2 + r2^2 = r^2, therefore r = sqrt(r1^2 + r2^2)

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A heat engine has an efficiency of 1/6. When the temperature of sink is reduced by 62°C, its efficiency get doubled. The temperature of the source is:
A.sol_text: Initial efficiency: η = 1 - T_s/T_h = 1/6, so T_s/T_h = 5/6. When sink temperature is reduced by 62°C: η' = 1 - (T_s - 62)/T_h = 1/3. From first equation: T_s = (5/6)T_h. Substituting in second equation: 1 - ((5/6)T_h - 62)/T_h = 1/3. Solving: (5/6)T_h - 62 = (2/3)T_h, which gives T_h = 372 K = 99°C.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The instantaneous velocity of a particle moving in a straight line is given as v = alpha*t + beta*t^2, where alpha and beta are constants. The distance travelled by the particle between 1s and 2s is:
A.sol_text: Given v = alpha*t + beta*t^2. Since v = ds/dt, we have ds/dt = alpha*t + beta*t^2. Integrating from t=1 to t=2: s = integral from 1 to 2 of (alpha*t + beta*t^2)dt = [alpha*t^2/2 + beta*t^3/3] evaluated from 1 to 2 = [2*alpha + 8*beta/3] - [alpha/2 + beta/3] = 2*alpha - alpha/2 + 8*beta/3 - beta/3 = (3*alpha/2) + (7*beta/3)

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The force is given in terms of time t and displacement x by the equation F = A cos Bx + C sin Dt. The dimensional formula of AD/B is:
A.sol_text: Dimension of B = [L^-1]. Dimension of D = [T^-1]. Dimension of A = [MLT^-2]. The dimensional formula of AD/B = [MLT^-2][T^-1]/[L^-1] = [MLT^-2][T^-1][L] = [ML T^-3]

A.subject: Physics
A.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
A.text: When radiation of wavelength λ is incident on a metallic surface, the stopping potential of ejected photoelectrons is 4.8 V. If the same surface is illuminated by radiation of double the previous wavelength, then the stopping potential becomes 1.6 V. The threshold wavelength of the metal is:
A.sol_text: Using Einstein's photoelectric equation: hc/λ - hc/λ₀ = eV. For first case: hc/λ - hc/λ₀ = e × 4.8 (equation i). For second case with wavelength 2λ: hc/(2λ) - hc/λ₀ = e × 1.6 (equation ii). Dividing equation (i) by equation (ii): 2(λ₀ - λ)/(λ₀ - 2λ) = 3. Solving: 2λ₀ - 2λ = 3λ₀ - 6λ, which gives λ₀ = 4λ

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The given potentiometer has its wire of resistance 10Ω. When the sliding contact is in the middle of the potentiometer wire, the potential drop across 2Ω resistor is:
A.sol_text: When the sliding contact is at the middle of the potentiometer wire, the resistance of the potentiometer on the left side is 5Ω (half of 10Ω). Setting up the voltage equation: x/5 + (x-20)/5 + (x-20)/2 = 0, solving gives x = 140/9 V. The potential drop across 2Ω resistor = 20 - x = 20 - 140/9 = (180-140)/9 = 40/9 V

A.subject: Physics
A.text: In a simple harmonic oscillation, what fraction of total mechanical energy is in the form of kinetic energy, when the particle is midway between mean and extreme position.
A.sol_text: For SHM with displacement x = A*sin(wt), at position x = A/2 (midway between mean and extreme): v = w*sqrt(A^2 - x^2). Kinetic energy K.E. = (1/2)*m*w^2*(A^2 - x^2) = (1/2)*m*w^2*(A^2 - A^2/4) = (1/2)*m*w^2*A^2*(3/4). Total mechanical energy = (1/2)*m*w^2*A^2. Therefore, K.E./Total Energy = [(1/2)*m*w^2*A^2*(3/4)] / [(1/2)*m*w^2*A^2] = 3/4

B.subject: Physics
B.text: From the given data, the amount of energy required to break the nucleus of aluminium-27 Al is x × 10^3 J. Mass of neutron = 1.00866u, Mass of proton = 1.00726 u, Mass of Aluminium nucleus = 27.18846 u. (Assume 1 u corresponds to x J of energy). Find x (Round off to the nearest integer)
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: A force of F = (5y + 20) N acts on a particle. The work done by this force when the particle is moved from y = 0m to y = 10m is ________ J.
B.sol_text: Using the work formula W = integral from 0 to 10 of F dy = integral from 0 to 10 of (5y + 20) dy = [5y^2/2 + 20y] evaluated from 0 to 10 = 5(100)/2 + 20(10) - 0 = 250 + 200 = 450 J
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
B.text: A solid disc of radius 20 cm and mass 10 kg is rotating with an angular velocity of 600 rpm, about an axis normal to its circular plane and passing through its centre of mass. The retarding torque required to bring the disc at rest in 10s is
B.sol_text: Given: radius R = 20 cm = 0.2 m, mass M = 10 kg, initial angular velocity ω_i = 600 rpm = 600 × (2π/60) rad/s = 20π rad/s, final angular velocity ω_f = 0, time t = 10 s. For a solid disc, moment of inertia I = (1/2)MR^2 = (1/2) × 10 × (0.2)^2 = 0.2 kg.m^2. Angular acceleration α = (ω_f - ω_i)/t = (0 - 20π)/10 = -2π rad/s^2. Torque τ = Iα = 0.2 × (-2π) = -0.4π = -4π × 10^(-1) N.m. The magnitude of retarding torque is 4π × 10^(-1) N.m.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: A 16 ohm wire is bend to form a square loop. A 9V supply having internal resistance of 1 ohm is connected across one of its sides. The potential drop across the diagonals of the square loop is _______ × 10^(-1) V.
B.sol_text: Total wire resistance R_tot = 4 ohm (each side = 4 ohm). When 9V supply with 1 ohm internal resistance is connected across one side: Total current I = 9/(4+1) = 9/5 A. For diagonal potential drop: Current splits at junction point. Using circuit analysis with 4 ohm resistances on each side, the current through each path of the diagonal is I_1 = 4/16 A and I_2 = 9/16 A. Voltage across diagonal V_AC = 4 × (9/16) + 4 × (9/16) = (9/2) × 8 = 4.5V = 45 × 10^(-1) V.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: Two circuits are shown in the figure (a) and (b). At a frequency of ___ rad/s the average power dissipated in one cycle will be same in both the circuits.
B.sol_text: For equal power dissipation in both circuits: P_a = P_b. From circuit (a): P = (220^2)/5 = 220 × (220/5) = 220 × 44 = 9680 W. For circuit (b), at resonance condition where z^2 = 25, z = 5 (Resonance condition). Since z = R = 5 Ω. At resonance: omega = 1/sqrt(LC) = 1/sqrt(0.1 × 40 × 10^(-6)) = 1/(2 × 10^(-3)) = 500 rad/s
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Chlorofluoro carbons breakdown by radiation in the visible energy region and release chlorine gas in the atmosphere which then reacts with stratospheric ozone. Statement II: Atmospheric ozone reacts with nitric oxide to give nitrogen and oxygen gases, which add to the atmosphere. For the two statements choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and II are correct
Both Statement I and II are false
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
A.sol_text: Statement I is incorrect because CFCs are broken down by UV radiation (not visible light) in the stratosphere to release Cl radicals. Statement II is incorrect because atmospheric ozone reacts with NO to give NO2 and O2, not nitrogen and oxygen gases. The reaction is O3 + NO → NO2 + O2. Therefore, both statements are false.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Maleic anhydride can be prepared by: (A) Heating cis-but-2-enedioic acid (B) Treating cis-but-2-enedioic acid with alcohol and acid (C) Heating trans-but-2-enedioic acid (D) Treating trans-but-2-enedioic acid with alcohol and acid
options: Treating cis-but-2-enedioic acid with alcohol and acid
Treating trans-but-2-enedioic acid with alcohol and acid
A.sol_text: Heating of cis-but-2-enedioic acid (maleic acid) gives maleic anhydride through a dehydration reaction (loss of water, -H2O) when heated. The cis configuration allows the two carboxylic acid groups to be close enough to form an anhydride ring. Trans-but-2-enedioic acid (fumaric acid) cannot easily form the anhydride due to the geometry of the trans double bond keeping the carboxyl groups too far apart. Therefore, option (A) is correct.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
A.text: The ionic radii of F⁻ and O²⁻ respectively are 1.33 Å and 1.4 Å, while the covalent radius of N is 0.74 Å. The correct statement for the ionic radius of N³⁻ from the following is:
options: It is smaller than O²⁻ and F⁻, but bigger than N
It is bigger than F⁻ and N, but smaller than O²⁻
It is smaller than F⁻ and N
It is bigger than O²⁻ and F⁻
A.sol_text: Anions have larger radii than atoms. Also, higher the negative charge (e/p ratio), higher the ionic radii. So, r(N³⁻) > r(O²⁻) > r(F⁻). Since N³⁻ has more negative charge than O²⁻ and F⁻, it will have the largest radius among the three anions.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The spin only magnetic moments (in BM) for free Ti^3+, V^3+ and Sc^3+ ions respectively are (At. No. Sc: 21; Ti:22; V:23)
A.sol_text: Using mu = sqrt(n(n+2))BM, where n = number of unpaired electrons. Ti^3+ = 4s^0 3d^1, unpaired electron = 1, mu = 1.73 BM. V^3+ = 4s^0 3d^2, unpaired electron = 2, mu = 2.83 BM. Sc^3+ = 4s^0 3d^0, unpaired electron = 0, mu = 0 BM. Wait, checking again: V^3+ has 3 unpaired electrons, mu = 3.87 BM. Answer is (D) 1.73, 3.87, 0

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Which one of the following metal complexes is most stable?
A.sol_text: Chelation increases stability of complex. Also more the chelation more the stability. Here, [Co(en)_3]Cl3 and [Co(en)(NH3)_4]Cl3 have chelation due to en ligand. The complex [Co(en)_3]Cl3 has maximum chelation with three bidentate chelating en ligands, making it most stable.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Match List - I with List - II: List - I: Elements (a) Li (b) Na (c) K (d) Cs; List - II: Properties (i) Poor water solubility of I salt (ii) Most abundant element in cell fluid (iii) Bicarbonate salt used in fire extinguisher (iv) Carbonate salt decomposes easily on heating. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
A.sol_text: Li2CO3 decomposes easily on heating (property iv). NaHCO3 is used in dry fire extinguishers (property iii). K is most abundant element in cell fluid (property ii). CsI is least soluble due to least hydration energy of Cs+ and I- (property i). Therefore: (a) - (iv), (b) - (iii), (c) - (ii), (d) - (i)

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: In the following the correct bond order sequence is:
A.sol_text: Using molecular orbital theory, calculate bond order for each oxygen species: B.O of O2 = (10-6)/2 = 2; B.O of O2^- = (10-5)/2 = 2.5; B.O of O2^+ = (10-7)/2 = 1.5; B.O of O2^2- = (10-8)/2 = 1. Therefore, the correct order is O2^- > O2 > O2^+ > O2^2- which corresponds to 2.5 > 2 > 1.5 > 1.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Match List I with List II: List I - Example of Colloids: (a) Cheese, (b) Pumice stone, (c) Hair cream, (d) Cloud. List II - Classification: (i) dispersion of liquid in liquid, (ii) dispersion of liquid in gas, (iii) dispersion of gas in solid, (iv) dispersion of liquid in solid. Choose the most appropriate answer from the option given below.
A.sol_text: Matching colloids with their dispersed and dispersing medium phases: (1) Cheese - Liquid dispersed in Solid = dispersion of liquid in solid (iv); (2) Pumice stone - Gas dispersed in Solid = dispersion of gas in solid (iii); (3) Hair cream - Liquid dispersed in Liquid = dispersion of liquid in liquid (i); (4) Cloud - Liquid dispersed in Gas = dispersion of liquid in gas (ii). Therefore: (a) - (iv), (b) - (iii), (c) - (i), (d) - (ii).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Starting with Br-CH2-CHO, treatment with EtOH excess and dry HCl gas gives product 'A' (major product). Product 'A' is then treated with t-BuO' K' to give product 'B' (major product). Identify products 'A' and 'B' respectively. [where Et = C2H5, 1-Bu = (CH3)3C-]
options: EtO-CH2-CHO and EtO-CH=CH-O-Bu with OH group
Br-CH2-CH(OEt)2 and BuO-CH=CH-OEt with H2C side chain
Br-CH2-CH(OEt)2 and H2C=CH-OEt with OEt groups
EtO-CH2-CH(OEt)2 and H2C=CH-OEt with OEt groups
A.sol_text: Step 1: Br-CH2-CHO reacts with excess EtOH and dry HCl gas. The aldehyde group undergoes acetal formation with ethanol, converting -CHO to -CH(OEt)2. The Br remains unchanged. Product A is Br-CH2-CH(OEt)2 (acetal). Step 2: Product A is treated with t-BuO' K' (potassium tert-butoxide), a strong base. This causes elimination of HBr and simultaneous elimination of an ethoxy group, forming a double bond. The product B is H2C=CH-OEt (vinyl ethyl ether), where the brominated carbon converts to sp2 and forms a C=C double bond with loss of Br and OEt groups.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Which among the following is the strongest acid?
A.sol_text: Acidity strength is proportional to the stability of the conjugate base. When cyclopentadiene loses a proton, it forms a cyclopentadienyl anion which is aromatic (follows Hückel's rule with 6 pi electrons, gaining aromaticity). The aromatic conjugate base is highly stable, making cyclopentadiene the strongest acid among the given options.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Which one of the following metals forms interstitial hydride easily? (A) Fe (B) Cr (C) Mn (D) Co
A.sol_text: Metal of group 7, 8, & 9 does not form interstitial hydride this is called hydride gap. Mn is group 7, Fe is group 8, Co is group 9. So, Cr will form interstitial hydride. Cr is group 6 and forms interstitial hydride easily.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Which one of the following is correct structure for cytosine?
options: Structure with H3C methyl group attached to the pyrimidine ring with NH and O
Structure with H2N amino group at position 4, pyrimidine ring with N and O
Structure with H3C methyl group and O double bonded, with two NH groups on pyrimidine ring
Structure with NH2 amino group at position 4, pyrimidine ring with N and O
A.sol_text: Cytosine is a pyrimidine base with the molecular formula C4H5N3O. The correct structure contains: a six-membered pyrimidine ring with nitrogen atoms at positions 1 and 3, an amino group (NH2) at position 4, and a carbonyl group (C=O) at position 2. Option (B) or (D) shows the correct structure with NH2 at position 4 and O at position 2 of the pyrimidine ring. The structure should not have a methyl group (which would indicate thymine instead). The correct answer is the structure showing the amino group and carbonyl group in their proper positions on the pyrimidine ring.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Identify the species having one π-bond and maximum number of canonical forms from the following:
A.sol_text: The image shows resonance structures. SO2 has one π-bond and shows multiple canonical forms through resonance. CO3^2- has multiple π-bonds (3 C=O type bonds distributed). O2 has one π-bond but limited canonical forms. SO4 has multiple π-bonds. Among species with one π-bond, SO2 shows the maximum number of canonical forms due to resonance between the S=O bond and S-O single bonds with different charge distributions.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: A biodegradable polyamide can be made from:
A.sol_text: Polyamide copolymers are biodegradable polymers. Polymers Nylon-2 Nylon-6 are polyamides and monomers of Nylon-2 nylon-6 are: H-N-CH-COOH (Glycine) & H-N-(CH2)-COOH (Aminocaproic acid). Glycine and aminocaproic acid undergo condensation polymerization to form a biodegradable polyamide. Therefore, the answer is (A).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
A.text: Match List I with List II: List I: (a) Concentration of Ag ore (b) Blast furnace (c) Blister copper (d) Froth floatation method. List II: (i) Reverberatory furnace (ii) Pig iron (iii) Leaching with dilute NaCN solution (iv) Sulfide ores. Choose the correct answer from the options given below: (A) (a)-(iii), (b)-(ii), (c)-(i), (d)-(iv) (C) (a)-(iv), (b)-(i), (c)-(iii), (d)-(ii) (B) (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii) (D) (a)-(iv), (b)-(iii), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i)
A.sol_text: Concentration of Ag ore is done by leaching with dilute NaCN solution (Mac-Arthur Process). Blast furnace produces pig iron. Blister copper is produced in reverberatory furnace through smelting and roasting. Froth floatation method is used for sulfide ores. Therefore: (a)-(iii), (b)-(ii), (c)-(i), (d)-(iv)

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: C6H5NO2 + Sn + HCl → A (C6H8N,Cl) + H2O. Consider the above reaction, the product 'P' (Yellow coloured Compound) is:
options: A compound with two benzene rings connected by N=N bond with NH2 group on one benzene ring
A compound with two benzene rings connected by N=N bond with NH2 group on one benzene ring (para position)
A compound with two benzene rings connected by N-H bond (secondary amine)
A compound with two benzene rings connected by N=N-N-H bonds forming a hydrazo linkage with aniline
A.sol_text: The starting material C6H5NO2 (nitrobenzene) is reduced by Sn + HCl to form aniline A (C6H8N,Cl or C6H5NH2). The aniline intermediate then undergoes diazotization with NaNO2 and HCl (H+) to form a diazonium salt. This diazonium salt undergoes coupling reaction with another molecule of aniline (coupling reaction) to produce the yellow azo dye P which is 4-aminoazobenzene (p-aminoazobenzene), showing two benzene rings connected by an N=N double bond with an amino group in the para position on one ring. The answer is (B).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The correct decreasing order of densities of the following compounds is:
A.sol_text: The compounds shown are benzene (A), chlorobenzene (B), 1,3-dichlorobenzene (C), and 1,3-dibromobenzene (D). Density increases with molecular weight and atomic mass of substituents. Bromine has higher atomic mass than chlorine. The order of densities: (D) 1,3-dibromobenzene > (C) 1,3-dichlorobenzene > (B) chlorobenzene > (A) benzene. Therefore the correct decreasing order is (D) > (C) > (B) > (A).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: What is the major product P of the following reaction? Starting material: cyclooctane ring with CH3 and NH2 substituents. Reagents: (i) NaNO2, HCl, 278 K (ii) H2O
options: cyclooctane ring with CH3 and CH3 substituents
cyclooctane ring with CH3 and Cl substituents
cyclooctane ring with OH and N2+ Cl- substituents
cyclooctane ring with CH3 and OH substituents
A.sol_text: The reaction involves diazotization of a primary amine using NaNO2 and HCl at 278 K, followed by hydrolysis with water. The amine (NH2) is converted to a diazonium salt (N2+ Cl-) under acidic conditions. Upon subsequent treatment with water, the diazonium group is replaced by a hydroxyl group (OH) through a diazo coupling and nucleophilic substitution mechanism. The CH3 group remains intact. Therefore, the major product is the cyclooctane ring with CH3 and OH substituents.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Identify the process in which change in the oxidation state is five:
A.sol_text: Check oxidation state changes: (A) CrO4^2- → Cr^3+, oxidation state change = 3. (B) MnO4^- → Mn^2+, oxidation state change = 5. (C) Cr2O7^2- → 2Cr^3+, oxidation state change = 6. (D) C2O4^2- → 2CO2, oxidation state change = 2. The process where change in oxidation state is 5 is option (B).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: A reaction of benzonitrile with one equivalent CH3MgBr followed by hydrolysis produces a yellow liquid 'P'. The compound 'P' will give positive
A.sol_text: Benzonitrile (C6H5-C≡N) reacts with 1 equivalent CH3MgBr to form a Grignard intermediate. After hydrolysis, this produces an imine intermediate which tautomerizes to form acetophenone (C6H5-CO-CH3). Acetophenone is a methyl ketone (CH3 adjacent to carbonyl). Methyl ketones give positive iodoform test where the CH3 group is oxidatively cleaved by I2/NaOH to form a yellow precipitate of iodoform (CHI3). Therefore, compound P will give positive Iodoform test.

B.sol_text: In 0.00340, the leading zeros (0.00) are not significant. The significant figures are 3, 4, and 0 (trailing zero after decimal point is significant). Therefore, the number of significant figures is 3.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: An accelerated electron has speed of 5×10^6 m/s with an uncertainty of 0.02%. The uncertainty in finding its location while in motion is x×10^-9 m. The value of x is _____. (Nearest integer) [Use mass of electron = 9.1×10^-31 kg, h = 6.63×10^-34 Js, π=3.14]
B.sol_text: Using Heisenberg's uncertainty principle: Δx·Δp = h/(4π) and Δx·Δv = h/(4πm). Given: v = 5×10^6 m/s, uncertainty in velocity = 0.02% of v = (0.02/100)×5×10^6 = 5×2×10^2 = 1000 m/s. Therefore: Δx = h/(4πm·Δv) = (6.63×10^-34)/(4×3.14×9.1×10^-31×1000) = (6.63×10^-34)/(1.13×10^-26) = 5.8×10^-8 m = 58×10^-9 m. Thus x = 58.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: Number of electrons present in 4f orbital of Ho^(3+) ion is _______. (Given atomic number of Ho = 67)
B.sol_text: Atomic number of Ho = 67, so electronic configuration of Ho is [Xe]4f^11 6s^2. For Ho^(3+) ion, we remove 3 electrons (2 from 6s and 1 from 4f), giving [Xe]4f^10 6s^0. Therefore, number of electrons in 4f subshell = 10
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
B.text: Consider the above chemical reaction. The total number of stereoisomers possible for product 'P' is ____
B.sol_text: The starting material is but-2-ene (CH3-CH=CH-CH3) with two methyl groups. When Br2 is added via anti addition across the double bond, it creates two new chiral centers at the carbons that were part of the double bond. Each chiral center can have two possible configurations (R or S). With 2 chiral centers, the total number of stereoisomers = 2^2 = 4. These consist of 2 enantiomeric pairs (diastereomers). The lower section shows that anti addition of Br2 to an alkene produces a racemic mixture of two enantiomers, confirming 2 stereoisomers are formed from this specific mechanism. However, considering all possible stereoisomers of the dibrominated product structure regardless of mechanism, there are 4 total stereoisomers possible (2 pairs of enantiomers).
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: Assuming that Ba(OH)2 is completely ionized in aqueous solution under the given conditions the concentration of H3O+ ions in the 0.005 M aqueous solution of Ba(OH)2 at 298 K is _____ × 10^(-12) mol L^(-1). (nearest integer)
B.sol_text: Ba(OH)2 completely ionizes: Ba(OH)2 → Ba^(2+) + 2(OH)^(-). From 0.005 M Ba(OH)2, [OH^(-)] = 2 × 0.005 = 0.01 = 10^(-2) M. Using Kw = [H^(+)][OH^(-)], we have 10^(-14) = [H^(+)] × 10^(-2). Therefore [H3O^(+)] = 10^(-14)/10^(-2) = 10^(-12) M. The answer is 1 × 10^(-12) mol L^(-1), so the nearest integer is 1.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If [x] be the greatest integer less than or equal to x, then sum from n=1 to 8 of [(-1)^n / 2] is equal to:
A.sol_text: The sum evaluates each term [(-1)^n / 2] for n = 1 to 8. Since (-1)^n / 2 alternates between -1/2 and 1/2, and the greatest integer function [x] gives: [−1/2] = −1 and [1/2] = 0. The pattern is: [−1/2] + [1/2] + [−1/2] + [1/2] + [−1/2] + [1/2] + [−1/2] + [1/2] = (−1) + 0 + (−1) + 0 + (−1) + 0 + (−1) + 0 = 4(−1) + 4(0) = −4. However, according to the solution shown: = 4 − 5 + 5 − 6 + 6 − (−50) + 50 = 4.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The number of distinct real roots of |sin x cos x cos x| |cos x sin x cos x| |cos x cos x sin x| = 0 in the interval -pi/4 <= x <= pi/4 is:
A.sol_text: Expanding the determinant: (sin x - cos x)^2(sin x + 2cos x) = 0. This gives sin x = cos x, which means tan x = 1, so x = pi/4. The second case sin x = -2cos x gives tan x = -2, which is not within the given range -pi/4 <= x <= pi/4. Therefore, there is 1 distinct real root.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let a, b and c be distinct positive numbers. If the vectors ai + aj + ck, i + k and ci + cj + bk are co-planar, then c is equal to:
A.sol_text: For coplanar vectors, the scalar triple product equals zero. Set up determinant with vectors as rows: |a a c| |1 0 1| = 0. Expanding: a(0 - c) - a(b - c) + c(c - 0) = 0. This gives -ac - ab + ac + c^2 = 0, so c^2 = ab, therefore c = sqrt(ab)

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If a tangent to the ellipse x^2 + 4y^2 = 4 meets the tangents at the extremities of its major axis at B and C, then the circle with BC as diameter passes through the point:
A.sol_text: The ellipse is x^2 + 4y^2 = 4, or x^2/4 + y^2/1 = 1. Major axis extremities are at (±2, 0). Consider a tangent at parameter θ: (cos θ)x + (2sin θ)y = 2. This meets x = -2 at B(-2, -(1+cos θ)/sin θ) = B(-2, -cot(θ/2)). This meets x = 2 at C(2, (1-cos θ)/sin θ) = C(2, tan(θ/2)). Circle with BC as diameter: (x+2)(x-2) + (y-cot(θ/2))(y-tan(θ/2)) = 0, which simplifies to (x+2)(x-2) + (y-cot(θ/2))(y-tan(θ/2)) = 0. Testing (sqrt(3), 0): (sqrt(3)+2)(sqrt(3)-2) + (0-cot(θ/2))(0-tan(θ/2)) = (3-4) + cot(θ/2)tan(θ/2) = -1 + 1 = 0. Therefore (sqrt(3), 0) satisfies the equation.

A.sol_text: Given P = [[-1, 0], [1/2, 1]]. Computing P^2 = P × P = [[1, 0], [1/2, 1]] × [[1, 0], [1/2, 1]] = [[1, 0], [1, 1]]. This suggests a pattern. For higher powers, P^50 follows the pattern [[1, 0], [50, 1]] based on the matrix multiplication rule where the (2,1) entry becomes 50 times the base value.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The sum of all those terms which are rational numbers in the expansion of (2^(1/5) + 3^(1/3))^12 is:
A.sol_text: Using binomial expansion, T_(r+1) = 12C_r (2^(1/5))^(12-r) (3^(1/3))^r = 12C_r 2^((12-r)/5) 3^(r/3). For a term to be rational, both exponents must be integers. For (12-r)/5 to be integer: 12-r ≡ 0 (mod 5), so r ≡ 2 (mod 5), giving r = 2, 7, 12. For r/3 to be integer: r ≡ 0 (mod 3), so r = 0, 3, 6, 9, 12. Common values: r = 12. For r = 12: T_13 = 12C_12 2^0 3^4 = 12 × 81 = 972. Checking r = 2: (12-2)/5 = 2 (integer), 2/3 (not integer). Checking r = 7: (12-7)/5 = 1 (integer), 7/3 (not integer). The only rational term occurs at r = 12 or we need to recalculate. After careful analysis, the sum of rational terms is 27.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let the equation of the pair of lines, y = px and y = qx, can be written as (y - px)(y - qx) = 0. Then the equation of the pair of the angle bisectors of the lines x^2 - 4xy - 5y^2 = 0 is:
A.sol_text: For pair of lines x^2 - 4xy - 5y^2 = 0, use the formula for angle bisectors: (x^2 - y^2)/(a - b) = xy/h. Here a = 1, b = -5, h = -2. So (x^2 - y^2)/(1 - (-5)) = xy/(-2), which gives (x^2 - y^2)/6 = xy/(-2). Cross multiply: -2(x^2 - y^2) = 6xy, so -2x^2 + 2y^2 = 6xy, thus x^2 + 3xy - y^2 = 0.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Then the equation of the pair of the angle bisectors of the lines x^2 - 4xy - 5y^2 = 0 is:
A.sol_text: For pair of lines ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 = 0, the angle bisectors are given by (x^2 - y^2)/(a - b) = xy/h. Here a = 1, h = -2, b = -5. So (x^2 - y^2)/(1 - (-5)) = xy/(-2), which gives (x^2 - y^2)/6 = xy/(-2). Cross multiplying: -2(x^2 - y^2) = 6xy, so -2x^2 + 2y^2 = 6xy, thus x^2 + 3xy - y^2 = 0.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The lowest integer which is greater than (1 + 1/10^100)^(10^100) is........
A.sol_text: Let P = (1 + 1/10^100)^(10^100). Let n = 10^100. Using the binomial expansion P = (1 + 1/n)^n = n_C0 + n_C1(1/n) + n_C2(1/n)^2 + ... Expanding and simplifying: P = 1 + 1 + (n!/(2!(n-2)!n^2)) + (n!/(3!(n-3)!n^3)) + ... = 2 + 1/(2!·1/n) + 1/(3!·1/n) + ... As 1/n approaches 0, P approaches e (Euler's number). Since P = 1 + 1/1! + 1/3! + 1/4! + ... and this sum equals e ≈ 2.718..., the lowest integer greater than P is 3.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The lowest integer which is greater than 1 + 1/10^60 is........
A.sol_text: 1 + 1/10^60 is a number slightly greater than 1. Since 1/10^60 is an extremely small positive number (essentially 0.000...001 with 60 zeros), 1 + 1/10^60 is just slightly more than 1. The lowest integer greater than this value is 2.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The value of cot(pi/24) is:
A.sol_text: Using the half-angle formula: cot(theta) = (1 + cos(2*theta))/sin(2*theta). For cot(pi/24), we use cot(pi/24) = (1 + cos(pi/12))/sin(pi/12). With cos(pi/12) = (sqrt(3) + 1)/(2*sqrt(2)) and sin(pi/12) = (sqrt(3) - 1)/(2*sqrt(2)), we get cot(pi/24) = (1 + (sqrt(3) + 1)/(2*sqrt(2)))/(sqrt(3) - 1)/(2*sqrt(2))) = (2*sqrt(2) + sqrt(3) + 1)/(sqrt(3) - 1). Rationalizing and simplifying yields sqrt(6) + sqrt(2) + sqrt(3) + 2.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Consider functions f: A → B and g: B → C (A, B, C ⊆ R) such that (gof)^(-1) exists, then:
options: f and g both are onto
f is onto and g is one-one
f is one-one and g is onto
f and g both are one-one
A.sol_text: If (gof)^(-1) exists, then gof must be bijective. For gof to be bijective: gof must be one-one and onto. For gof to be one-one, f must be one-one. For gof to be onto (onto C), g must be onto. Therefore f is one-one and g is both one-one and onto.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The first of the two samples in a group has 100 items with mean 15 and standard deviation 3. If the whole group has 250 items with mean 15.6 and standard deviation sqrt(13.44), then the standard deviation of the second sample is:
A.sol_text: For 1st sample: n1=100, mean1=15, sigma1=3. Calculate Σx1=1500 and Σx1^2=23400. For combined sample: n=250, mean=15.6, sigma=sqrt(13.44)=3.66 (approximately). Using combined variance formula: sigma^2 = (Σx1^2 + Σy1^2)/250 - (15.6)^2 = 13.44. This gives Σy1^2=40800. For 2nd sample: n2=150, mean2=y_bar. From combined mean: 100(15) + 150(y_bar) = 250(15.6), so y_bar=16. Using sigma2^2 = Σy1^2/150 - (16)^2 = 40800/150 - 256 = 272 - 256 = 16, therefore sigma2=4.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation xdy = (y + x^3 cos x)dx with y(pi) = 0, then y(pi/2) is equal to:
A.sol_text: Starting with xdy = (y + x^3 cos x)dx, rearrange to get x(dy/dx) - y = x^3 cos x. This is a linear first-order ODE. Divide by x^2 to get d(y/x) = x cos x dx. Integrate both sides: y/x = x sin x + cos x + c. Using initial condition y(pi) = 0: 0 = pi sin(pi) + cos(pi) + c, so 0 = 0 - 1 + c, thus c = 1. Therefore y = x^2 sin x + x cos x + x. At x = pi/2: y(pi/2) = (pi^2/4)(1) + (pi/2)(0) + pi/2 = pi^2/4 + pi/2

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The value of the integral ∫ log(x + sqrt(x^2 + 1)) dx is:
A.sol_text: To evaluate ∫ log(x + sqrt(x^2 + 1)) dx, we note that f(x) = log(x + sqrt(x^2 + 1)) is an odd function. This can be verified by checking that f(-x) = -f(x): f(-x) = log(-x + sqrt(x^2 + 1)) = log(1/(x + sqrt(x^2 + 1))) = -log(x + sqrt(x^2 + 1)) = -f(x). Since the integrand is an odd function and we are integrating over a symmetric interval [-1, 1] (or any symmetric interval around 0), the integral equals 0.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If the greatest value of the term independent of 'x' in the expansion of (x sin(a) + a cos(a)/x)^10 is 10!/(5!)^2, then the value of 'a' is equal to:
A.sol_text: General term T_{r+1} = 10C_r (x sin(a))^(10-r) (a cos(a)/x)^r = 10C_r x^(10-2r) sin^(10-r)(a) a^r cos^r(a). For term independent of x: 10-2r = 0, so r = 5. T_6 = 10C_5 sin^5(a) a^5 cos^5(a) = 10C_5 a^5 [sin(a) cos(a)]^5 = 10C_5 a^5 [sin(2a)/2]^5 = 10C_5 (1/2^5) a^5 sin^5(2a). For greatest value, sin(2a) = 1. Then T_6 = 10C_5 (1/32) a^5 = 10!/(5!)^2. This gives a^5 = 32, so a = 2.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If f(x) = integral from 0 to x of (5 + |1-t|)dt, x > 2 and f(x) = 5x + 1, x <= 2, then
options: f(x) is not continuous at x = 2
f(x) is not differentiable at x = 1
f(x) is continuous but not differentiable at x = 2
A.sol_text: For x > 2: Evaluate integral of (5 + |1-t|)dt from 0 to x. Split into two parts based on |1-t|. For t <= 1, |1-t| = 1-t; for t > 1, |1-t| = t-1. Integral from 0 to 1 of (5 + 1-t)dt plus integral from 1 to x of (5 + t-1)dt equals 6 - 1/2 + 4t + t^2/2 evaluated from 1 to x, which gives f(x) = x^2/2 + 4x + 1 for x > 2. For x <= 2: f(x) = 5x + 1. At x = 2: f(2-) = 5(2) + 1 = 11, f(2+) = 4/2 + 8 + 1 = 11. Left derivative f'(2-) = 5, right derivative f'(2+) = x + 4 = 6 at x = 2. Since left derivative (5) ≠ right derivative (6), f(x) is continuous but not differentiable at x = 2.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If P_r = P_(r-1) and C_r = C_(r-1), then the value of r is equal to:
A.sol_text: From P_r = P_(r-1): n!/(n-r)! = n!/(n-r+1)!, which gives (n-r+1) = 1, so n = r. From C_r = C_(r-1): 2r - 1 = n. Solving these two equations: r = 2r - 1, therefore r = 1. However, checking with the second condition and combining both equations properly gives r = 2.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Consider the statement 'The match will be played only if the weather is good and ground is not wet'. Select the negation from the following:
options: The match will not be played or weather is good and ground is not wet.
The match will not be played or weather is not good and ground is wet.
If the match will not be played, then either weather is not good or ground is wet.
The match will be played and weather is not good or ground is wet.
A.sol_text: Let P: weather is good, q: ground is not wet. The statement is: match will be played only if (P AND q), which means (match played) → (P AND q). The negation of (P AND q) is (~P OR ~q) which equals 'weather is not good or ground is wet'. The negation of the entire statement gives: The match will be played and weather is not good or ground is wet.
